title: The two Texturelabs plates
note: The film frame and the paper tile the Effect Stack draws. Both leave here centred on mid-grey, which is the decision the rest of the pipeline hangs off: overlay and soft-light are no-ops at exactly 128, so the flat field costs nothing and only the marks land. The stack's own numbers - strength, blend, lift, contrast, size - are Tokens under kernel-effects and move live; these are what is IN the picture.
needs: Texturelabs_Film_185XL.jpg and Texturelabs_Paper_349XL.jpg in design/effects/sources/. They are 9 MB and 12 MB, gitignored under texturelabs.org's own licence, and free downloads from there.

groups.name: What is being baked
groups.note: The two are entirely different jobs: the film is used ONCE, stretched over the whole band, because the marks on it are singular events; the paper is cut small and tiled, and carries no marks at all.

params.label: which plate
params.note: `all` is both. Baking one is about twenty seconds and baking both is under a minute.

groups.name: The film - 185XL, one frame
groups.note: A high-pass at a tenth of the frame takes its gross shape off - its overall blackness and its corner falloff - which is far larger than any mark on it, so every scratch, speck and bloom comes through untouched. Without it the texture stops being a texture and starts being a vignette painted over the page.

params.label: inset
params.note: How much of each edge is cropped off before anything else, to lose the plate edge the scan carries.

params.label: high-pass radius
params.note: As a fraction of the frame. Larger keeps more of the frame's own shape; smaller starts eating the marks.

params.label: grain kept
params.note: The fine detail the high-pass leaves, before the gain below.

params.label: gain
params.note: How far what is left is pushed away from mid-grey. The band's own standard deviation is about seven levels once the grain is out, so this is what makes a scratch visible at all.

params.label: gamma
params.note: Open, and more open than the paper's: what is left here is events rather than field.

params.label: WebP quality
params.note: Lossy on purpose: a full-frame wash at 18% opacity or less, where an artefact arrives at a fifth of its strength.

groups.name: The paper - 349XL, tiled
groups.note: Most of build-textures.py is about making this WRAP. The mottle is low-frequency, and there a slow light-to-dark drift is worse than ugly: the drift itself is the seam, so removing it at a small radius is what makes the seamless step possible at all rather than merely tidier.

params.label: crop, x and y
params.note: Where in the sheet the tile is cut from, as two fractions of it. Two numbers in one control because it is one decision about one point, and build-textures.py reads it out of the parameters file rather than off a command line.

params.label: cut at
params.note: The square taken out of the source, in source pixels, before it is made to wrap and resampled down to the rungs.

params.label: tile size
params.note: The tile's own size. --fx-paper-size in kernel-effects is how big it is DRAWN, and that one is live.

params.label: high-pass radius
params.note: In tile pixels, and small: the fibre is what is wanted and the mottle is what is not.

params.label: gain
params.note: As the film's, against a field that is already mid-grey rather than nearly black.

params.label: gamma
params.note: Tighter than the film's: this one is asked only to put a tooth on the page.
